150:     this.publish({ mode: "battle", from, to, effectiveThreshold, lastOutcome, rolls, ties, attackerWins, defenderWins, message });
151:     return true;
152:   }
153: 
154:   singleExchange(revision?: number): boolean {
155:     if (!this.accepts(revision) || this.current.running || this.current.paused || !this.canExchange()) return false;
156:     this.exchange(false);
157:     return true;
158:   }
159: 
160:   fightOn(revision?: number): boolean {
161:     if (!this.accepts(revision) || this.current.running || !this.canExchange()) return false;
162:     this.watchExchanges = 0;
163:     this.current = { ...this.current, effectiveThreshold: this.current.paused ? this.current.effectiveThreshold : this.clamp(), paused: false };
164:     this.exchange(true);
165:     return true;
166:   }
167: 
168:   /** Called once per chosen exchange, never to prepare a later exchange. */
169:   private exchange(continuous: boolean): void {
170:     const from = this.current.from!, to = this.current.to!;
171:     const before = this.state;
172:     const result = apply(before, { kind: "attack", from, to });
173:     if (!result.ok || !result.outcome) return;
174:     const rolls = exchangeRolls(before, from, to);
175:     const outcome = result.outcome;
176:     this.watchExchanges += 1;
177:     const captured = result.state.pendingCapture !== undefined;
178:     const exhausted = armyCount(result.state, from) < result.state.rules.combat.minArmiesToAttack;
179:     const threshold = armyCount(result.state, from) <= this.current.effectiveThreshold;
180:     const running = continuous && !captured && !exhausted && !threshold && result.state.phase === "attack";
181:     // Queue only after this outcome exists. A stop invalidates even a callback
182:     // already removed from the scheduler's queue (covered by the stale-callback test).
183:     if (running) this.schedule();
184:     this.publish({ state: result.state, lastOutcome: outcome, rolls, running, paused: false,
185:       ties: this.current.ties + rolls.reduce((n, roll) => n + roll.results.filter(r => r === "tie").length, 0),
186:       attackerWins: this.current.attackerWins + outcome.defenderLosses,
187:       defenderWins: this.current.defenderWins + outcome.attackerLosses,
188:       message: captured ? "Captured. Choose how many armies move in." : exhausted ? "Stopped: only one army remains at the source." : continuous && threshold ? `Stopped at ${this.current.effectiveThreshold} armies.` : running ? "Fighting on. Stop before the next exchange at any time." : "One exchange complete.",
189:     });
190:   }
191: 
192:   private schedule(): void {
193:     const own = this.generation;
194:     const scale = SPEED_SCALE[this.current.speed];
195:     this.timer = this.scheduler.schedule(() => {
196:       if (this.disposed || own !== this.generation) return;
197:       this.timer = null;
198:       if (!this.current.running || !this.canExchange()) return;
199:       // The same 12 fully shown exchanges at every speed; the 13th needs consent.
200:       if ((this.watchExchanges + 1) * EXCHANGE_TIME * scale > HUMAN_BATTLE_WATCH * scale) {
201:         this.publish({ running: false, paused: true, message: "Battle paused. Keep watching or stop with these stacks." });
202:         return;
203:       }
204:       this.exchange(true);
205:     }, EXCHANGE_TIME * scale);
206:   }
207: 
208:   stop(revision?: number): boolean {
209:     if (!this.accepts(revision) || (!this.current.running && !this.current.paused)) return false;
210:     this.cancel();
211:     this.publish({ running: false, paused: false, message: "Stopped. Both countries keep their current armies." });
212:     return true;
213:   }
214: 
215:   confirmCapture(amount: number, revision?: number): boolean {
216:     if (!this.accepts(revision) || !this.pending()) return false;
217:     const result = apply(this.state, { kind: "captureMove", amount });
218:     if (!result.ok) return false;
219:     this.cancel();

221:     return true;
222:   }
223: 
224:   dispatch(action: Action, revision?: number): boolean {
225:     if (!this.accepts(revision) || this.pending() || this.current.running || this.current.paused) return false;
226:     if (action.kind === "captureMove") return false;

233:       return this.singleExchange(revision);

241:     });

```typescript
private clickProvince(id: string, inspect = false): void {
```

```typescript
private clickProvince(id: string, inspect = false): void {
    if (this.disposed) return;
    const { state, from, to, mode, running, paused } = this.controller.view;
    if (this.computerActive() || running || paused || state.pendingCapture || state.phase === "finished" || state.phase === "human-loss") return;
    ...
```

When the click returns early due to running/paused, the clickProvince doesn't call select or singleExchange. But the BattleController already has these guards. So this is defense in depth.

Let me also check what happens during pause. In paused mode, the BattleController blocks singleExchange via `!this.canExchange()` which checks `!this.pending()`. Actually no, canExchange checks `this.current.running || this.current.paused || ...`. So it returns false during pause. select() also checks `this.current.running || this.current.paused`. Let me consolidate and write the final review now.

One more thing - let me check the correct details on my independent mutation. Let me verify the test failures actually demonstrate the breakage.

Looking at my mutation - I inverted the inspect parameter at the call site:
```
onProvince: (id, activation) => { if (!activation?.repeat) this.clickProvince(id, activation?.inspect ?? false); },
```
became:
```
onProvince: (id, activation) => { if (!activation?.repeat) this.clickProvince(id, !(activation?.inspect ?? false)); },
```

With my mutation:
- Normal click: activation.inspect = false (no Shift) → clickProvince(id, true) → inspect=true → !inspect=false → singleExchange NOT called
- Shift click: activation.inspect = true (Shift) → clickProvince(id, false) → inspect=false → !inspect=true → singleExchange called

So Shift+click would attack, normal click would just select. This breaks:
- Mouse enemy activation test (because normal click doesn't attack)
- Keyboard attacks agree test (because Enter/Space doesn't attack)
- Shift-click retains separate controls test (because Shift+click attacks)

6 tests failed across 3 test names × 2 viewports. Restoration verified.
